caption:
Anthropic just opened the door for regular investors.

The Claude maker says up to 20% of its IPO could go to retail investors, at an expected $70 to $78 a share. Brokers including Fidelity, Robinhood, Schwab, SoFi and E*TRADE are taking requests, and trading on Nasdaq under ANT could start as early as November 19.

A request does not guarantee shares, and the opening price can land above or below the range. This is news, not investment advice.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, said in an updated regulatory filing on November 10, 2026, that up to 20% of the shares in its initial public offering could be allocated to retail investors, according to Yahoo Finance. The company plans to offer 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an expected price of $70 to $78 per share. At the top of that range the offering would be worth up to $64.35 billion.

Anthropic also shared a link to a dedicated IPO website, ipo.anthropic.com, in a post on X, along with a notice that it has filed a registration statement and prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission and that investors should read the prospectus before investing.
How retail investors can request shares

Eligible customers of Fidelity, Robinhood, Charles Schwab, SoFi and E*TRADE can request shares through those brokers, CoinCentral reported on November 12, 2026. Fidelity customers must submit an indication of interest before an expected deadline of November 17. A request does not guarantee an allocation if demand is higher than the number of shares available, and access varies by country, the outlet said.

Outside the United States, a report by MarsBit republished by KuCoin said the IPO website has regional paths for the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, and named Interactive Brokers, Revolut and SBI as participating institutions. That report cites unnamed filings and has not been confirmed by Anthropic.

Pricing is expected on November 18, and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT could begin as early as November 19, according to CoinCentral, which noted that the dates can change and that the opening price could land above or below the expected range. Yahoo Finance estimated the retail portion at about $12.2 billion at the $74 midpoint.

The filing shows third quarter revenue of $17 billion, more than 12 times the figure a year earlier, and more than 11,900 customers that spend at least $100,000 a year, Yahoo Finance reported. It also lists about $900.9 billion in committed spending, most of it for computing infrastructure, with about $451.6 billion expected before the end of 2030.

Retail investors received about 20% of SpaceX's offering as well, Yahoo Finance said, citing The Wall Street Journal. That stock priced at $135, opened at $150 and passed $200 by its third day, and was later trading below $150. Facebook opened at $38 on May 17, 2012, and was under $18 by early September of that year.

In NeuraFeed's reading, a large retail allocation does two things at once. It lets the people who use Claude every day own a piece of the company on the same terms as institutions, and it moves part of the first-day price risk onto buyers who have the least information. The SpaceX and Facebook examples show that a strong opening and a lower price a few weeks later can both happen to the same stock. The size of Anthropic's spending commitments, more than fifty times its latest quarterly revenue, is the number in the filing that deserves the most attention from anyone weighing a request.
Watch the final price set on November 18 and how many shares retail investors actually receive, since both will show how much demand exists outside the large funds before trading begins.
